info.name: Demo Flow — Register, Login, Trade
info.description:
One straight-through demo path, in the order to click them in: register a user, log in, check starting balance/holdings, look up a live AAPL quote from Fauxnance, place a BUY order for AAPL, then watch it resolve. No collection/environment variables anywhere — every URL and body is a literal value. Two things need to be copied by hand as you go (noted on each request below):

1. **The access token** — copy the `accessToken` field from the '2 - Login' response into the `Authorization` header of every request after it (they all currently say `Bearer PASTE_ACCESS_TOKEN_HERE`).
2. **The order price** — request 6 fetches AAPL's live quote; request 7's price (1000.00) is already set comfortably above any realistic ask so the BUY fills, but if you want, check the quote's `ask` field and adjust the price in request 7 to be at or above it (FillRule only fills a BUY when the limit >= ask).

**Prerequisites:**
- The stack must be running locally: `./run-local.sh start` (trade-api on :8085, auth-service on :3000).
- Run the requests top to bottom, in order — later ones depend on earlier responses.
- `accountId: 1` throughout is the seeded ACTIVE demo account (₹100,000 starting cash). A token is only valid for the account it was issued for — using it against account 2 or 3 gets `403 ACC-403`.
- Re-running '1 - Register' a second time with the same username gets `409` (username taken) — change the username (and re-run login) if you need a fresh run-through. Re-running '7 - Place Order' with the same `idempotencyKey` gets `409 ORD-409` — change `idempotencyKey` for a fresh order.

request.description: Expect { "status": "UP", ... }. If this doesn't respond, start the stack first: ./run-local.sh start

Creates a login (username/password) linked to trade-api's existing account 1 (ACC-10001, ACTIVE, seeded with ₹100,000). This does NOT create a trading account — accountId must already exist in trade-api, which it does for account 1.

Expect 201 with the created user: { id (uuid), username, accountId: 1, roles: ["CUSTOMER"], createdOn }.

No token is issued here — log in next.

If you've already run this once against the current database, you'll get 409 (username already taken): change "username" to something new and proceed.

Expect 200 with { accessToken, refreshToken, tokenType: "Bearer", expiresIn: 900 }.

COPY the accessToken value now — paste it in place of PASTE_ACCESS_TOKEN_HERE in every request from here on (their Authorization header reads "Bearer PASTE_ACCESS_TOKEN_HERE"). It's a 15-minute token; log in again if it expires mid-demo.
Optional but a good demo beat: proves the token actually works and shows who it identifies. Expect 200 with { id, username: "demo.trader", accountId: 1, roles: ["CUSTOMER"], createdOn }.

Expect 200 with { accountId: 1, cashBalance, currency: "INR", asOf }. Account 1 is seeded with ₹100,000 starting cash, but on a shared/already-used database cashBalance may already be lower from earlier trading activity — note whatever value comes back here and compare it against request 9 after the order fills (it should drop by roughly executedPrice × 5).

Expect 200 with an array of this account's current holdings. On a fresh seed this is just the seeded TCS position; on a shared/already-used database there may be others too — either way, there should be no AAPL entry yet. Compare against request 10 after the order fills, where an AAPL entry should appear (quantity 5, or +5 if you've run this flow before and already hold some).

Direct call to the live Fauxnance sandbox (not through trade-api/executor) — the same source the executor polls for fill pricing. Expect 200 with { data: { symbol: "AAPL", price, bid, ask, ... }, meta: {...} }.

Note the "ask" value: request 7's BUY only fills if its price is at or above this ask (FillRule). The 1000.00 default in request 7 is comfortably above any realistic AAPL ask, but you can tighten it to just above this response's "ask" for a more realistic demo price.

Expect 200 immediately with status "NEW" — the fill/reject decision happens asynchronously (the executor polls Kafka roughly every couple of minutes locally, per POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS). Wait a bit, then check request 8 to see it resolve to FILLED.

idempotencyKey is a fixed literal ("demo-flow-order-001") — change it before re-running this request, or you'll get 409 ORD-409 instead of a fresh order.

Expect 200 with an array of this account's orders, newest included. Look for idempotencyKey "demo-flow-order-001" — status should have moved from NEW to FILLED (or REJECTED/NO_PRICE_AVAILABLE if Fauxnance couldn't price it). Re-run this request a few times a bit apart if it's still NEW — the executor's poll interval means the fill isn't instant.
Compare against request 4: cashBalance should have dropped by (executed_price × 5), matching the fill seen in request 8.
Compare against request 5: should now show { accountId: 1, symbol: "AAPL", quantity: 5, averageCost }, closing out the demo.
